title: Fake Microsoft Store Pages Deliver a RAT That Lets Attackers Watch and Control Windows PCs
content_md: A campaign uses fake Microsoft Store product pages to trick Windows users into installing legitimate remote-management software. Attackers then use that access to deploy AgtaBackup RAT, a custom .NET malware strain that can steal browser data, record keystrokes, capture screens, and run commands without the user seeing them. Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 reported the campaign on September 28. The attack starts with a page advertising popular video-conferencing software. It looks like a Microsoft Store listing, but its download delivers a genuinely signed remote monitoring and management (RMM) installer, such as LogMeIn Resolve or ConnectWise ScreenConnect, rather than the promised application. Fake Microsoft Store Spreads RAT The victim sees a normal installer and a Windows User Account Control (UAC) prompt. If they approve it, the RMM service enrolls the PC in an attacker-controlled account. Its traffic goes to the RMM vendor’s legitimate cloud service, which can make the access look routine. Hours or days later, the attacker opens a remote terminal through that RMM connection. A PowerShell command downloads AgtaBackupAgent.msi from attacker-controlled infrastructure and installs it silently. The RAT lands under C:\Program Files\Agta Backup\ as Credential Guard.exe , a name chosen to resemble a Windows security component. It runs as a hidden SYSTEM service called AgtaBackupAgentSvc .
